faq: Why different text for each store?

Apple indexes a hidden keyword field and a subtitle, while Google reads the full description for search. So we write for each store's way of working, while keeping your brand voice consistent across both.
Do you use real screens from my app?
Yes, from a real build, with captions and clean frames. We never show features the app does not have. Send a build or screens and we make the sizes both stores require.
Can you promise a better ranking or more installs?
No. Store ranking depends on installs, ratings, retention and competition. We make your pages clear, accurate and policy compliant, but we cannot promise a position or download numbers.
Do you need access to both consoles?
Only if you want us to enter the text for you. We ask for limited roles in App Store Connect and Play Console, never passwords. Otherwise we send a ready-to-paste document.
desc:
App Store and Google Play listings for Flutter apps give each store a page written to its own rules. Ecom Swift LLC writes the titles, descriptions, keywords and screenshots, then enters everything in your own developer accounts.

## What is an app store listing?

An app store listing is the public page of your app on the App Store or Google Play. It holds the name, subtitle or short description, full text, screenshots, icon, category, age rating and privacy details. For many people it is the first and only thing they see before deciding to install.

A Flutter app produces one codebase, but it has two listings, because each store has its own fields, limits and review process.

## Why one listing does not fit both stores

The two stores work differently. Apple gives you a title, a subtitle, a keyword field and promotional text. Google Play gives you a title, a short description and a long description that the store reads for search. Image sizes, feature graphics and privacy forms also differ.

Copying one text into both loses value on each. A subtitle written for Apple may not fit Google's short description, and keywords placed in a field that Apple hides do nothing on Google, where the visible text matters. Each store also has metadata policies that prohibit claims such as misleading comparisons or pricing in the title.

## How a clear listing affects results

A listing works on two levels. First, it helps people find the app: the right words in the right fields tell each store what the app is about. Second, it helps visitors decide: screenshots, a clear first line and an honest description answer the question "is this what I need?".

When both are done well, more of the right people open the page and install. We cannot promise rankings or install numbers, since competition, category, reviews and ads all play a part. What we can do is remove avoidable mistakes and give each store what it expects.

## What a strong store listing includes

- A title and subtitle for the App Store, using the words people actually search.
- A title and short description for Google Play within its character limits.
- Full descriptions that open with the main benefit and explain features in plain language.
- App Store keywords chosen without repeating words from the title.
- Screenshots from your real app, in the sizes each store requires, with short captions.
- A Google Play feature graphic that matches your brand.
- Promotional text and a clear "What's new" note for updates.
- A correct category and age rating.
- A review of the Apple privacy label and the Google Data safety form against what the app really does.
- Optional tablet images, translated text and a preview video storyboard in higher packages.

## How we prepare your listings

We start with your app and your audience. We install the app, study how people use it and review a handful of similar apps to find the language buyers use. From that we draft the store texts, one version for each store, and send them for your approval.

Next we produce screenshots from real screens, add captions, and prepare the Google Play feature graphic in the Standard and Premium packages. We check the privacy answers with you against the data the app collects, so the forms are accurate. When everything is approved, we enter it into App Store Connect and Google Play Console from a team or developer user in your own accounts. The Premium package adds more screenshots, tablet images, two translations and a plan for testing listing variants. The stores' reviewers decide approval, so we write to the published guidelines and avoid claims they ban.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Start the description with what the app does for the user.
- Use screenshots that show real features, not just decorative art.
- Keep the privacy answers consistent with the app's behavior.
- Update the "What's new" text with every release.
- Check each store's current character limits before editing.

**Avoid:**
- Stuffing keywords into the title or description.
- Naming competitors or using their trademarks.
- Promising features the app does not have.
- Showing devices or content that you do not have the rights to use.
- Copying the same text to both stores.

## Who this service is for

An owner about to publish a first Flutter app who wants both pages ready. A team whose app has been live for a while but whose listing has never been improved. A business that needs a language version for a new market.

## What we need from you

A short description of your app and audience, access to the app or a test build, your icon and brand colors, and a team or developer user in App Store Connect and Google Play Console. We never ask for passwords. We share all drafts for approval before anything is entered.
